sources.title: Jumlah Tindak Pidana ... Menurut Kepolisian Daerah Menurut Kabupaten/Kota di Provinsi Jawa Barat, 2023
sources.representation: Researcher-authored audit receipt with attributed metadata/short excerpts
sources.evidence: Rendered table obtained after browser hydration. Last updated 20 February 2025. Actual first-column header is Satuan Wilayah Hukum, not civil administrative geography. Rows include Polda Jawa Barat and 23 named resort units; three further rows have blank labels and unavailable values. Police-reported totals and rates are readable, but no numerical observations are stored because civil mapping and rate denominator fail acceptance. Notes claim Polresta Bandung combines Kabupaten Bandung, Kabupaten Bekasi, Kota Bekasi and Kota Depok; notes also combine Cimahi/Bandung Barat and Ciamis/Pangandaran although Pangandaran has its own row. These notes are unresolved, not an endorsed crosswalk. A generic kabupaten/kota title does not resolve these contradictions.

polresta Cimahi = Kota Cimahi + Kab. Bandung Barat
polres Ciamis = Kab. Ciamis + kab. Pangandaran

sources.title: Statistik Potensi Desa Provinsi Jawa Barat 2024, general explanations and security technical notes
sources.representation: Researcher-authored audit receipt with attributed metadata/short excerpts
sources.evidence: Executive summary printed vii / PDF 9 dates the census to May 2024. General explanations printed xxiv–xxv / PDF 26–27 establish civil census scope, definitive operational administrative areas with clear boundaries, and direct interviews by trained BPS staff/partners with knowledgeable responsible local informants plus related documents. Paragraph 6 explicitly lists Table 18.4 among tables referring to one year before enumeration; therefore this is preceding-year recall at May 2024, not calendar-year 2023. Chapter 18 technical notes printed 183 / PDF 211 define crime broadly, including attempts; selected column is theft and excludes the separately listed robbery column. These are village occurrence indicators, not numbers of incidents, police reports, victims or exposed residents.

candidates.title: Desa/kelurahan with theft occurrence during the year preceding Podes May 2024 enumeration
candidates.publisher: Badan Pusat Statistik Provinsi Jawa Barat
candidates.referencePeriod: Podes 2024: one year preceding May 2024 enumeration (not calendar 2023)
candidates.geographicLevel: Civil kabupaten/kota aggregation of desa/kelurahan occurrence reports
candidates.definition: Number of desa/kelurahan in each civil kabupaten/kota where theft (Pencurian, Table 18.4 column 2) occurred during the year before enumeration. This counts village-level presence, not police reports, incidents, victims or residents. Robbery (Pencurian dengan Kekerasan) is a separate column and is not added.
candidates.numerator: Source-published count of desa/kelurahan reporting theft occurrence in the preceding year.
candidates.denominator: None: absolute village/kelurahan count. No population or village-share rate is constructed.
candidates.measurementMethod: Podes 2024 civil administrative census, enumerated May 2024. Trained BPS personnel/partners directly interviewed relevant knowledgeable, authorized local informants and examined related documents. General explanations paragraph 6 explicitly assigns Table 18.4 to the preceding-year reference period. BPS publishes the kabupaten/kota aggregation; no police jurisdiction crosswalk is used.
candidates.missingness: All 27 selected theft-column cells are published numeric counts; no selected cell is blank or a missing-value symbol. No filling, imputation or forced zero occurs. Presence of a published count does not establish complete detection of underlying crime.
candidates.updateFrequency: Podes major census three times per decade; this publication reports the 2024 round. Publication catalogue also labels release frequency annual; do not infer annual comparable theft observations.
candidates.licenseOrUsageNotes: Current BPS website section 13 explicitly permits commercial/noncommercial statistical-data use, copying/distribution and extraction with BPS credit, content title, access date, direct original link, lawful use and no false endorsement. PDF page 4 separately prohibits partial/full commercial book reproduction without written permission. Audit relies only on the explicit current statistical-data extraction grant for narrowly attributed factual cells; it does not redistribute the PDF, layout, images or full table text. Conflicting publication notice remains a downstream commercial-reuse review caveat; no open licence is fabricated.

comparability.reason: All 27 civil-region counts use one BPS Podes census, one selected category and one recall period; civil administrative scope is explicit in method. Raw village counts vary with numbers and sizes of villages, local recall and detection, so this audit disables cross-region ranking and risk comparisons.

knownBiases: Local-informant awareness, recall, record access and willingness to disclose affect reported occurrence.
Unreported or undetected theft can be missed; occurrence is not police-recorded incidence.
One village with one incident and one village with many incidents each contribute one to the published count.
Regions differ in village/kelurahan counts, village population and geographic size; raw counts are not a risk rate.
limitations: Nearby-year context, not an actual calendar-2023 police-crime measure.
Method states one year before May 2024 enumeration but does not supply exact day-level start/end dates; no artificial calendar boundaries are imposed.
Only theft column is transcribed; no all-crime total is obtained by adding overlapping crime categories.
Canonical IDs are assigned from explicit civil BPS administrative scope and unambiguous regency/city labels; source table supplies names, not machine-readable region codes.
No denominator rate, population-risk estimate, ranking, danger classification, resident-stress inference or CORE integration is supported.
Current website extraction grant and older PDF commercial reproduction notice must both remain visible in downstream rights review.
candidates.recommendedUse: Dated, attributed village-safety context only: display published theft-occurrence village count with its Podes period and method. Keep separate from police-reported crime, resident safety risk and frozen CORE scores. Do not rank regions.
candidates.decisionReason: All 27 factual theft-village counts are directly read from primary BPS Table 18.4; civil aggregation, unit, recall period and method resolve. Current BPS terms explicitly permit attributed statistical-data extraction; publication-specific reproduction caveat is disclosed. Accepted only as nearby-year village occurrence context, never a police-crime or resident-risk panel.
safeStatements: In Podes 2024, BPS recorded desa/kelurahan with theft occurrence during the year preceding May 2024 enumeration.
These values count villages/kelurahan with occurrence, not theft incidents or affected people.
unsafeStatements: These are calendar-year 2023 police-recorded crime counts.
This number is the count of theft incidents or victims.
Higher counts mean residents are more unsafe or stressed.
This is the percentage or probability of residents experiencing crime.
Adding the crime-type village counts gives distinct villages with any crime.
statementTemplates: BPS Podes 2024 recorded {value} desa/kelurahan in {regionName} with theft occurrence during the year preceding May 2024 enumeration; this is not an incident count or resident-risk rate.
candidates.temporalWarning: Collected in May 2024; Table 18.4 refers to the preceding year. Do not relabel this recall window as calendar 2023 or align it mechanically with 2023 CORE values.
